Last month, we sent the Intendant general of Cuba, "Don Felipe Fernandez de Castro" to Haiti in a diplomatic mission to retrieve the eastern side of Hispaniola, which we lost 9 years ago. Sadly, the Haitian officials didn't seem to reason with us, arguing that our claim had lost legitimacy after the criollos overthrew the colonial government, but also even going as far as to say that our efforts to reestablish Spanish rule over the old empire was a "lost cause". De Castro left the island enraged and threatening the Haitian government with an invasion. It's now up to us whether to follow up on his words.

\n\nPresident Jean-Pierre Boyer addressed the Haitian people today with a proclamation about a recent meeting with representatives of Spanish Crown. As the meeting consisted of a Spanish request to the return Santo Domingo to Spain, a request which would be deeply unconstitutional to obligeâ€”the proclamation reassured the territorial integrity of the Republic. He reminded our people of our great union and reminded the people of the Eastern District that they joined Haiti willingly, urging them to remain at rest in our government that seeks only to bring them happiness and prosperity. In the end, Boyer's message is clearâ€”we will remain firmly committed to the territorial integrity of Haiti as a whole. Naturally, following his adress to the nation, Boyer took measures to East Haiti from its Spansish roots, persecuting symphatizers of Fernando VII and stripping the region of its Spanish symbols.

\n\nDue to the chaos of the Napoleonic Wars in Spain, many of its Colonies pursued greater autonomy or independence. In 1814, the restored Spanish king, Ferdinand VII, declared the developments in the Americas illegal and sent armies to quell the areas still in rebellion. The restoration was short lived, reversed by 1820 and Spain has lost almost all of its territories in the New World, but he has maintained hope in eventually recovering them. All his attempts prior to this point have been in vain, but the recent Reconquest of Santo Domingo has convinced many in the court that peharps the tide is turning in our favor. Even if the king doesn't live for much longer, we can continue expanding on his efforts to reestablish the old Empire, but we have to do it quick

\n\nIn January of 1830 the Kingdom of Spain sent a diplomatic mission with the intent of forcing us to cede over the eastern side of Hispaniola, and after our humble refusal they decided to scalate the dispute into an all-out war. Fortunately, we have managed to repeal any Spanish attempt at gaining a foothold in the island and they're now suing for peace, showing the world that no one can threathen our territorial integrity.

Unfortunately, They have not only managed to land near Santo Domingo but also to crush the bulk of our army in one military engagement, forcing us to sign a peace treaty where we renounce our rights to the Spanish Santo Domingo.

\n\nIt is still unclear to us wether it was our navy being in a deplorable state or our troops not having a good morale, but our attempts at succesfully invading Hispaniola have failed. With no many resources left for a new attempt, we had no other choice than to recognize Haitian rule over the whole island. A humiliation for what was once a great empire.
